sm.text:

fluctuate based on the timing of our investments in consumer acquisition and retention. We continuously evaluate the impact

of sales and marketing activities on our business and actively manage our sales and marketing spend, including investment

in consumer acquisition, which is largely variable, as market and business conditions change.

change was also driven by a $12.6 million increase in advertising expenses, $11.0 million increa se in third- party marketing

expenses, and a $5.0 million increase in restructuring related costs . The impact from these drivers was partially offset by a

$27.1 million decrease in promotional expenses substantially in the form of consumer discounts.

sm.heading: Sales and marketing
sm.text:
Sales and marketing expenses are primarily driven by investments to grow and retain our consumer base and may

fluctuate based on the timing of our investments in consumer acquisition and retention. We continuously evaluate the impact

of sales and marketing activities on our business and actively manage our sales and marketing spend, including investment

in consumer acquisition, which is largely variable, as market and business conditions change.

Sales and marketing expenses increased $25.8 million , or 8% , year-over-year primarily driven by a $21.8 million

increase in payroll and related costs, principally due to higher average headcount and higher stock-based compensation

expense , due to a reversal in 2023 of previously recognized stock-based compensation expense as certai n performance

milestones were no longer probable of being met in addition to changes in our employee composition. The year-over-year

change was also driven by a $12.6 million increase in advertising expenses, $11.0 million increa se in third- party marketing

expenses, and a $5.0 million increase in restructuring related costs . The impact from these drivers was partially offset by a

$27.1 million decrease in promotional expenses substantially in the form of consumer discounts.

ga.heading: General and administrative
ga.text:
General and administrative expenses are primarily driven by changes in headcount and investments to support our

compliance and reporting obligations as a public company. General and administrative expenses may vary from period to

period based on the timing and extent of business mergers, acquisitions and dispositions, to support our organic growth, and

financing activities. Impairments and disposals of long-lived assets may also cause general and administrative expenses to

General and administrative expenses decreased $7.7 million , or 6% , year-over-year, primarily driven by a $16.1 million

decrease in stock-based compensation expense related to awards granted to our Co-Founders in 2020 and a $3.0 million

decrease in professional fees. The impact from these drivers was partially offset by a net $12.9 million increase in an

estimated loss with respect to ongoing class action litigations.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense decreased by $3.8 million , or 7% , year-over-year, primarily due to lower average debt balances ,

partially offset by higher interest rates.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
In 2024, we had an income tax expense of $15.1 million compared to an income tax benefit of $46.7 million in 2023 and

an effective income tax rate of 47.9% and 84.0% , respectively. The year-over-year change in our income taxes was primarily

due to the tax benefit recognized in 2023 from the release of our valuation allowance against our beginning of the year net

deferred tax assets in excess of tax amortizable goodwill. This was partially offset by a decrease in excess tax effects from

equity awards, tax effects from nondeductible officers' compensation and an increase in U.S. federal research and

development tax credits. For information regarding our valuation allowance analysis, see Part II, Item 7, "Management’s

Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates—

Income Taxes—Valuation of Deferred Tax Assets" and Note 11 in the notes to our audited consolidated financial statements

included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
